text:
Sam S. (Support): Heads-up — customer acct ACCT-478 (multi-entity) is hitting two issues: they need invoices in local currency for each legal entity (EUR for EU Ops, GBP for UK Subsidiary) and we're seeing FX rounding differences between invoice totals and payment amounts. Also their last card attempt failed. PO required for the EU entity. Can finance/payments advise next steps?

Maria F. (Finance): Can you drop the invoice IDs + account id and the customer's exact request? Are they asking for separate invoices per legal entity (one EUR, one GBP) or a single combined invoice with currency lines?

Sam S. (Support): Paste from the support thread:
```
customer: needs separate invoices for EU (VAT registered) and UK (local VAT), must show amounts in local currency on each invoice. they also require a PO number on the invoice header. last invoice numbers: INV-2024-0478 (EUR) and INV-2024-0479 (GBP). account: ACCT-478
card decline: last attempt 2024-03-16T15:12Z, decline code: card_declined, reason: avs_mismatch. customer insists bank reconciles to local currency amounts — small 0.01–0.05 differences cause them to reject payment.
```

BillingBot: invoice INV-2024-0478 created (EUR 1,234.56 / GBP 1,082.34) — fx_rate 1.1400 applied at 2024-03-16T14:04:12Z. tax_lines: VAT 20% applied to EU entity. PO field empty.

Maria F. (Finance): Thanks. A few things: 1) We need to confirm whether our billing pipeline issues separate legal-entity invoices (it can, but usually requires the account to be mapped to distinct billing entities). 2) FX rounding: our system currently rounds at line-item level to 2dp, but depending on conversion ordering that can lead to 0.01–0.05 discrepancies vs customer's bank. 3) PO requirement — we can add PO to header for future invoices but must reissue for closed invoices.

Kai L. (Sales): Customer signed SOW for multi-entity billing. They explicitly required local-currency invoices and PO on file. We already captured VAT reg number for EU entity. They will not accept a combined invoice.

Eve P. (Payments): For the card decline: AVS mismatch often from billing address vs card issuer country. Ask the customer to confirm billing address or try reprocessing with card on file after updating address. If they insist on bank transfer, we can provide GBP/EUR wired invoices. For immediate resolution we can: 1) issue a credit for the rounding delta, 2) reissue invoices with PO and local currency/legal entity breakdown, 3) rerun charge (with their permission).

Maria F. (Finance): Proposal: manual workflow: - Create new invoices per legal entity with PO number in header and explicit VAT lines. - Calculate FX using end-of-day rate and store rate on invoice metadata to avoid differences at reconciliation. - Issue a one-time credit memo equal to rounding difference (small amounts) so their reconciliation matches. - For recurring future invoices, update account mapping to generate separate local-currency invoices automatically.

Sam S. (Support): Customer ok with reissue + credit as long as we provide docs for reconciliation. They want: invoice PDFs showing PO, explicit VAT registration number on EU invoice, and the exchange rate used.

Maria F. (Finance): Action items: @Eve P. (Payments) to retry charge after address confirmation or advise bank transfer instructions. @Kai L. (Sales) can you confirm legal-entity IDs & PO format we should print? @Sam S. (Support) please collect cardholder confirmation and send updated billing address if available. I'll create reissued invoices and a credit memo draft and attach PDFs.

Eve P. (Payments): Will try to reprocess if they provide updated AVS info. If card still declines we'll mark payment pending and accept wire — email payments@redwood.com for bank details.

BillingBot: payment_attempt for INV-2024-0479 failed (card_declined) at 2024-03-16T15:12:31Z. charge_id ch_3KX...; decline_code: avs_mismatch.

Maria F. (Finance): Note for engineering/finance infra: we should track FX rate source (provider + timestamp) on all multi-currency invoices and add a rounding_tolerance metadata field. Filing a ticket to reduce/reconcile line-item rounding imprecision and expose the rate on invoice PDF.

Sam S. (Support): Customer asked whether we can apply a tolerance threshold so micro-diffs are auto-adjusted. They're concerned about automated rejections in their AP system.

Maria F. (Finance): Short-term: manual credit + reissue. Medium-term: engineering ticket to change rounding to aggregate-then-round vs line-item rounding and surface rate + tolerance. I'll open FINENG-2893 and link here.

Kai L. (Sales): I'll get the PO format and entity legal names. Also will check contract to confirm who pays bank fees for wire transfers.

Sam S. (Support): I'll update the customer with next steps and ETA (credit memo + reissues within 48h once PO & entity mapping confirmed). Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Maria F. (Finance): Thanks — keep this thread updated. If we need to expedite credits, ping me directly.
